what: Alcon makes eye care products. One half sells the equipment and intraocular lenses used in cataract and vision correction surgery; the other sells contact lenses and eye drops. It was spun out of Novartis in 2019.
customers: Eye surgeons and hospitals, optometrists, and consumers buying contact lenses and dry-eye drops.
money: cataract equipment, intraocular lenses and surgical consumables
contact lenses and ocular health products
moat: Surgical equipment placed in operating theatres that then consumes its own lenses and disposables, with surgeons trained on its systems.
risks: Cataract procedure volumes depend on hospital capacity and reimbursement
Return on invested capital of about 4% is low for a medical device company
Chinese government procurement has pushed down lens prices
Debt of about $5 billion against $2 billion of cash
opportunities: The population needing cataract surgery grows every year as people live longer
Premium intraocular lenses, paid for privately, earn far more than standard ones
Gross margin of 55% with steady mid-single-digit growth
watch: Surgical equipment placements and premium lens adoption rates.
